tasha (sales): Samir from the POC reports they can't correlate Redwood traces with their S3 logs because trace IDs are missing, and they're hitting occasional 429s. Can we swarm?

diego (solutions): On it. Samir, paste a tiny log sample and what shipper you use.

samir (client): Fluentd sidecar -> S3. Sample: 
2026-03-18T14:02:01Z INFO request path=/v1/chat status=200 trace=-
2026-03-18T14:02:02Z ERROR upstream status=429 trace=-
We do set X-Trace-Id in client.

nina (eng-infra): Two likely culprits: header not forwarded through LB/proxy or the fluentd parser/filter not mapping headers into the record. Which LB/proxy?

samir (client): ALB -> nginx in pod. Custom Go client.

diego (solutions): Quick fixes: (1) nginx: proxy_set_header X-Trace-Id $http_x_trace_id; add it to access_log format. (2) app middleware to attach header to structured JSON log. (3) fluentd record_transformer to copy headers.x-trace-id -> trace_id.

nina (eng-infra): Also increase fluentd buffer_chunk_limit and buffer_queue_limit to avoid drops during bursts; and ops can temp bump tenant rate while they validate.

ops-bot: Ops ticket OPS-3101 created to bump acme-tenant quota from 120->480 rps for 90 minutes.

samir (client): I pushed nginx change and updated fluentd filter. Smoke shows local logs include trace id now. Running load in 5m, will post S3 keys if any objects still missing trace_id.

diego (solutions): We'll watch Redwood console for X-Trace-Id and verify correlation once you upload.

(10m)

samir (client): Uploaded s3 keys: pocs/acme/2026-03-18/part-0009.gz — it now has "trace_id":"acme-0001". 429s dropped after client concurrency tuning + temp bump.

tasha (sales): Great. Ops will auto-revert. Samir please confirm once you run final validation and we'll close the blocker.

samir (client): Confirmed. All good. Thanks for the quick help.

diego (solutions): Following up with a short runbook (nginx + app middleware + fluentd mapping + buffer knobs). Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
